rationale: Correct the existing ownership record rather than preserve a false historical Acadia ownership claim. Current official Matrix disclosures identify Northleaf Capital Partners as the minority investor and Class A investor in the Stillhouse TEP LLC tax partnership, while Acadia is described as sourcing preferred equity and facilitating the environmental-attribute transaction. Matrix acquired and remains sponsor of the project. The correction removes Acadia from the ownership record, attributes the current minority interest to Northleaf without inferring a percentage or fund, keeps the project active, clarifies the description and financing milestone, and installs direct current ownership evidence as the primary citation. A fresh acquisition-and-exit search found no Northleaf disposition or signed exit.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Stillhouse is a utility-scale solar project in Bell County, Texas. Its customer base is the ERCOT market and contracted corporate offtakers, including Hyundai affiliates under a long-term power purchase arrangement. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted generation model centered on long-lived photovoltaic infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 210 megawatt AC and approximately 281 to 284 megawatt DC solar facility that reached completion in 2025 and commercial operations in 2026. Matrix Renewables acquired the late-stage project from OCI in 2023 and remains the project sponsor. Northleaf Capital Partners became a minority investor through the Stillhouse TEP LLC tax partnership in 2024; Acadia Infrastructure Capital sourced preferred equity and facilitated an environmental-attribute transaction but is not identified as an owner.
